purpose: Crosswalk from CIP funding-source labels to BeTH ledger funds and to a legal restriction class. Determines whether money in a CIP line could lawfully be redirected to street rehabilitation.
method: restriction_class is taken ONLY from a researched legal_basis in BeTH's 106-fund ledger or a cited statute/measure. Where BeTH's ledger records 'Not yet researched', the class here is 'unknown' and the amount is NOT redirectable for dashboard purposes. Fund type (enterprise, special revenue) is recorded as a signal but is NOT by itself treated as proof of restriction.

classes.voter_approved_tax: Parcel tax, sales tax or similar approved by voters for a stated purpose. Redirection generally requires another vote.
classes.enterprise_fund: Ratepayer money in a self-supporting fund. Generally restricted to the enterprise; Proposition 218 and bond covenants may apply.
classes.internal_service: Charges collected from other City funds to fund a specific service. Not general revenue.
classes.grant_condition: External grant with conditions and clawback risk.
classes.state_restricted: State-allocated revenue with statutory use limits (for example gas tax, vehicle registration fee).
classes.unrestricted: No identified legal restriction. Requires an affirmative citation, never an absence of evidence.
classes.unknown: Not yet researched. DEFAULT. Treated as not redirectable.
classes.council_discretionary: General Fund money appropriated to a capital fund. Council can redirect it by budget action, but encumbered amounts are contracts and paving amounts are bound by the Measure FF maintenance-of-effort floor.

mappings.evidence: BeTH ledger legal_basis not yet researched for the sewer fund. Sewer charges are ratepayer revenue and Proposition 218 almost certainly applies, but BeTH has not cited the authority.

BeTH ledger, researched: 'Enterprise fund; four State DBW loans (1964, 1971, 1985, 2001)'. The 2001 Harbor Construction 5 loan has $5,415,120 outstanding at 2025-06-30 through FY2041. The California Division of Boating and Waterways reviewed fund use in June 2023.
mappings.note: The Marina Fund is a net recipient of support, not a source. Its FY2028 projected balance is negative.

mappings.evidence: BeTH ledger, researched: 'Special parcel tax (two-thirds vote); rate $0.2652 per square foot of improvements' after the Measure Y increase.
mappings.note: Two-thirds voter approval for a stated purpose. Redirection to streets would require another vote. The fund also carries $281,500,000 of unfunded parks and camps capital need.

mappings.evidence: BMC Chapter 7.11 (citizens' initiative, Nov 5, 2024; Ordinance 7,952-N.S., Dec 10, 2024). Proceeds in a special fund "to be used only for" street, sidewalk and path repair, safety and environmental enhancements (7.11.010(E)); allocation approximately 45% streets / 15% sidewalks / 30% safety / 10% environmental (7.11.020(C)); Council cannot alter the allocation or the non-FF street funding floor without voters (Section 7(a)(3)-(4)). Not the same as fund 164 "Measure FF - Public Safety" (2020) or the 2008 library bond.
mappings.note: Cannot be redirected outside its voter-approved purposes. The adopted five-year program puts ~45.6% into street rehabilitation against an allocation of "approximately" 45%. Whether Council could put more Measure FF money into paving without a vote is an unresolved legal question; BeTH states no amount. See phase2/07-street-funding-legal-analysis.md.

mappings.evidence: BeTH ledger legal_basis 'Not yet researched'. Alameda County transportation sales tax; the local streets and roads category name implies street use, which would make it already committed to the purpose in question.
BeTH ledger legal_basis 'Not yet researched'. Likely gas tax or SB1 subject to statutory street and road use limits.
Alameda County vehicle registration fee. BeTH has not cited the enabling measure or its use limits.
BeTH ledger legal_basis 'Not yet researched'. Property-owner contributions for sidewalk repair; almost certainly restricted to that purpose.

FY2025 ACFR balance sheet (PDF p.75): fund balance $23,831,669 = restricted $7,771,575 (equal to notes receivable, not cash) + assigned $16,060,094 (incl. $4,491,447 encumbered). Assigned = intent by Council or City Manager, changeable by Council. Funded by a discretionary General Fund transfer (budget-adoption p.167).
mappings.note: Redirectable by Council, but 88% of FY2027 fund 501 appropriations ($10,412,200 of $11,885,200) is already paving. The rest is $1,473,000 a year of facility, sidewalk and park repairs: a gross conditional deferral ceiling of $2,946,000 over FY2027-28 ($2,916,000 excluding a contractual JPA contribution). Appropriations, not verified available cash. See phase2/data/street-funding-sources.json.

BeTH ledger legal_basis 'Not yet researched'. Clean Storm Water is an enterprise fund; a Proposition 218 assessment is likely.

mappings.note: Internal service balances have been used as one-time General Fund support elsewhere in Berkeley. The Workers' Compensation Fund shows the consequence: net position of -$9,752,938 at FY2025. Treat any proposal to redirect replacement reserves as creating a deferred liability, not as free money.

mappings.evidence: BeTH ledger, researched: 'Enterprise fund; rates set by Council under Proposition 218 majority-protest procedures'.

summary.headline: Of 15 CIP funding sources, BeTH has a researched legal basis for 6. One (CIP Fund 501) is redirectable by Council, and 88% of its FY2027 money is already paving. Measure FF is voter-restricted; its allocation is fixed by the ordinance, and whether more of it could go to paving is unresolved. The other 9 sources are not yet researched and are treated as not redirectable.
